(Photo courtesy of the Guam Department of Labor)

Government of Guam agencies are bracing for a shortage of H-2B construction workers after federal approvals slowed to a trickle this summer, the Guam Department of Labor said Friday.

Labor Director David Dell'Isola said roughly 1,200 foreign workers are on island, down from more than 1,700 a year ago, and that several military and civilian projects could be delayed.

The department will host a job fair next month at the University of Guam to recruit local residents into apprenticeship programs.
